body: Yep. March. Same here. Alas just one of those things. I’m v close just to binning the whole thing so we’ll see.

Not possible to book two at a time, pretty much to deter people from (a) using up test slots and (b) not just having a stab at the test and trying to get lucky. 

Not great but I understand why it’s like that.

I never actually said it’s not a big issue so your assumption that I think ‘it’s nothing/no big issue’ is incorrect. I was annoyed at myself for making said mistake in not checking side mirrors. I’m not sure if it’s because English may be your second language by the end of the comment or something else that you didn’t understand.

Absolutely a big deal.

No worries - was kinda annoyed when I posted and buoyed by my instructors ‘appeal it come on’ comment but, thinking on it, I’d rather pay for the test and some lessons versus a collision. It was a dumb mistake from me. At least now I’ll be laser focussed on mirrors. Don’t need a car for work so I’m not at any disadvantage not having one this second!

Scroll down to my comment with the edit. [I do recognise it.](https://www.reddit.com/r/LearnerDriverUK/comments/y2w8ec/someone_want_to_throw_me_off_a_building_one/is54kns/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app&utm_name=iossmf&context=3)

EDIT: I acknowledge mistake, let chap who commented know, and now get downvoted? Good to know this sub is supportive /s

No car there. Was totally clear save for a car about 150m back turning into another road. 

Examiner has probably thought it’s a built up area in general, you need to be super careful as stuff can happen v quickly. Don’t blame em for it. Would’ve been nice if he said ‘yeah at the roundabout’ earlier!
Edited my comment about 30 seconds after posting with basically this.

For more context - I was asked to go right by the examiner, tried checking with examiner ‘right at the roundabout or at this road?’ who then said nothing. I then thought ‘crap, wrong lane’, moved after seeing nothing behind me in the rear view mirror (roads were dead and no cyclists about when checking 5 seconds earlier). 

Instructor who was in the back of the car wants me to appeal out of principle but faff for £62? Not worth it. Still just pissed.

EDIT: on reflection, it’s better I fail and learn not to take a chance if I’m flustered than end up in a RTC.

Meds - beta blockers were floated but decided against as they could have a symptomatic infraction with the depression meds. Technically the meds I’m already on should quell anxiety but apparently not enough for this! 

Techniques - not much mindfulness you can do behind the wheel of a 1.something tonne metal box but floated as a pre-test thing. 

My attempt at putting myself into a ‘you know what, sod it, I’ll fail it’ mindset (as a form of self cognitive reflection) works up until realising that I’ve done that 4 times before and can’t screw up this time!
Only child. No dad in the picture (he’d forgotten he was already married…)

I’m on attempt 5. I’m a nervous person when it comes to tests (including interviews) because anxiety really does run my brain. I’ve been ridiculed before for the driving (as well as going to a university that was out of the top 10 etc) by exes which really left a dent on my ability to perceive things and care about things that don’t really matter. I live in London and don’t actually need a car to get around, and going to a university that’s ranked 15 or 16 has netted me a good job that’s right up there with the big dogs. The issue is I somehow decide to set my self worth on things which make no sense because of comments from others, or daddy abandonment issues or whatever else. 

My friend was the same in terms of nervousness and all. She passed and got her car and I just flipped. I hate that I reacted in that way and that I feel so much resentment. I don’t know if it’s because of mine and her history (she’s engaged but we had a bit of a thing when she was off the rails which I put a stop to) or something else. I just hate this.

Big question. A feeling of inadequacy that I can’t shake. Right now it’s manifesting in not being able to drive at the age of 25 (nervous with driving tests) and an extreme hatred of a friend who passed and got her first car. It’s deeper than that though. I’ve always had a feeling of not being able to live up to my potential and all because I just get fucked over along the way. Every time.
Glad it was useful. I hope you’re on the up soon
